text:
maria: Support reporting a spike of 5xx/timeouts hitting hosted inference /v1/generate since ~00:30 UTC. ~60 customer tickets so far, several complaining about socket timeouts. Escalating to war room.
ops-bot: ALERT: Increased 5xx rate on hosted-inference-prod. p90 latency up 4x in eu-west-1. Traces attached: https://internal/traces/abc123 :warning:
devon: I'm on it. Can someone drop a quick repro from a failing request example? Need headers and payload sizes.
support-bot: Pasted one anonymized failing request: ``POST /v1/generate Authorization: Bearer <redacted> Content-Length: 9842 body: {"prompt":"long conversation...","max_tokens":1024}`` client saw 504 after 28s.
sophie: Thanks. I'm seeing a cluster of long-seq requests (seqlen > 4k) with streaming enabled. Batcher metrics show per-batch token count spike at 00:29 UTC.
alex: Any recent deploys around that time?\/ Did canary run?
devon: No deploys to runtime in that window. There was a minor change to edge LB config at 00:25 (increase keepalive) — checking if that correlates.
li: Attaching quick log excerpt from gateway: ```
[00:29:40] upstream response timeout to runtime-12 (POST /v1/generate)  - downstream client=10.2.5.3
[00:29:42] retrying request due to 504
[00:29:59] circuit-breaker tripped for runtime-12: consecutive_timeouts=6
```
devon: Circuit breaker tripping is interesting — could be backend intermittency or kv-cache warmup causing high latencies. Can we toggle fallback to a smaller quantized variant for affected routes?
sophie: We can flip fallback to model-small for the route within 2 mins, that'll reduce avg latency. Also recommend temporarily lowering batch window from 40ms -> 20ms to reduce head-of-line.
maria: Do it. Notify customers. @support-bot prepare a status line.
alex: Before changes, let's snapshot current traces and pprof. devon, can you run `curl -X GET https://runtime-metrics/internal/pprof snapshot` and upload?
devon: Running now. Uploading: https://internal/artifacts/pprof-1711112222.tar.gz
sophie: Patch applied: route fallback -> model-small, batch_window_ms=20. Observing p95 drop in eu-west within one minute. 5xx rate halved in first 3 minutes.
ops-bot: NOTE: mitigation deployed by sophie at 00:34 UTC — fallback enabled, batch_window reduced. Monitoring.
maria: Good. Support comms: "We applied a temporary mitigation to reduce latency; engineering investigating root cause. We'll follow up with full postmortem and action items"
support-bot: Status update posted to customers. Thread: https://status/redwood/incident/1711112222
devon: Preliminary root cause hypothesis: KV cache warmup + sudden influx of long-sequence streaming requests overloaded a subset of runtimes, causing upstream timeouts and circuit breakers that amplified failures due to fanout. Need to validate with host-level metrics.
sophie: Action items (short):
- Collect complete runtime host metrics for affected hosts (CPU, memory, GPU utilization, nvlink) — devon (ETA 4h)
- Add telemetry to measure seq-len distribution per route (PR: #4215) — sophie (ETA 3d)
- Improve KV cache warmup: pre-warm on scale-up + fallback to cached prefix when cold — eng-runtime (owner tbd) (ETA 2w)
- Evaluate dynamic batch window based on seqlen histogram — infra (owner li) (ETA 1w)
- Postmortem write-up and customer comms follow-up — maria (ETA 24h)
maria: Assigning owners in internal tracker. Any objections?
li: I'll take dynamic batch window task. I'll start with a small canary for eu-west.
devon: I'll gather metrics and try to reproduce with replay tooling, focusing on long streaming sequences + warm cold cache.
sophie: Also flagging SDK clients: some clients use aggressive retries which amplify retries when runtime is slow. Recommend a temporary guidance note to set retry backoff and not to retry 504s immediately.
maria: Great. Closing war room for now — mitigation is active, monitoring ongoing. We'll reconvene if 5xx rate rises. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: WARROOM CLOSED (mitigation active). Incident channel will remain open for postmortem updates.
